root_cause: Auth_Bypass (case-sensitivity mismatch lets a hop-by-hop Connection token strip Traefik-managed forwarded identity headers; CWE-178 / CWE-348)

v0.ref: pkg/middlewares/forwardedheaders/forwarded_header.go: XForwarded.ServeHTTP has NO removeConnectionHeaders — the Connection header is left intact, so Go's httputil.ReverseProxy strips whatever Traefik-managed header a client names hop-by-hop (e.g. `Connection: X-Real-Ip`). CVE-2024-45410.

v1.ref: CVE-2024-45410 fix (release v2.11.9): added XForwarded.removeConnectionHeaders, which recognizes Traefik-managed headers and drops their tokens from Connection so the header survives. BUT the guard `slices.Contains(xHeaders, sf)` compares the Connection token CASE-SENSITIVELY against canonical names (xHeaders holds `X-Real-Ip`), while the fall-through `req.Header.Del(sf)` and Go's header map delete CASE-INSENSITIVELY. A lowercase token `x-real-ip` misses the guard yet still deletes X-Real-Ip (CVE-2026-29054).

v2.ref: CVE-2026-29054 fix (release v2.11.38): removeConnectionHeaders now canonicalizes the token first (`key := http.CanonicalHeaderKey(sf)`) and checks `slices.Contains(xHeaders, key)` — so a lowercase token is recognized as protected -> X-Real-Ip survives -> bypass closed.

With the header present (Traefik's real external client IP) it returns 'forbidden'.

The flag returns iff a hop-by-hop Connection token successfully removed Traefik's X-Real-Ip.
